g.data-info: Large central region of parenchyma, well developed in monocot roots.
Parenchyma lying between the xylem and phloem groups.
Many xylem groups, each with small protoxylem outside and a large metaxylem vessel inside (exarch).
Phloem patches that alternate with the xylem groups on separate radii.
Thin-walled layer inside the endodermis from which lateral roots develop.
Barrel-shaped cells with a Casparian strip that control water entry into the stele.
Broad zone of parenchyma between the epiblema and the endodermis.
Outer single layer of thin-walled cells that bears root hairs and absorbs water.
Fine extensions of epiblema cells that take up water and minerals from the soil.
